section_summary: This section moves from international whaling rules to correspondence about Japan's supervised 1946–47 Antarctic whaling expedition, including its inspectors, catch reports, tanker conversion and flag. It also contains weekly reports on coastal catches and fleet readiness, correspondence about Japanese fisheries publications, and the opening pages of a glossary of Japanese fisheries terms.

subfiles.title: Whale definitions from whaling regulations
subfiles.about: Defines whale categories and alternative common names used in the preceding regulations.
subfiles.summary: Concludes definitions of sei, gray, humpback, right and sperm whales, plus an unclaimed dead whale.

subfiles.title: Protocol for the Regulation of Whaling
subfiles.about: Extends the 1945 whaling protocol to the 1947–48 season.
subfiles.summary: The Washington protocol substitutes the 1947–48 season and 1948 dates into the 1945 London protocol. It takes effect upon acceptance by all parties to the earlier protocol.

subfiles.title: Request to declassify Japanese Fishing Industry
subfiles.about: The War Department requests declassification of a 1945 publication on Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: Witsell asks permission to declassify Foreign Economic Administration's Japanese Fishing Industry.

subfiles.title: Referral of declassification request
subfiles.to: Mr. Emerson, Division of Japanese Affairs
subfiles.about: Requests review of the proposed removal of the publication's Confidential classification.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a copy of Japanese Fishing Industry and asks that it be returned after review.

subfiles.title: Reply on declassification of Japanese Fishing Industry
subfiles.about: Advises that the State Department has no objection to declassifying the publication.
subfiles.summary: Responds to Witsell's December 6 request with State's lack of objection.

subfiles.title: Questions about the Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Asks about whaling practice, inspectors, catch reports and a tanker conversion.
subfiles.summary: Graves seeks assurance that the expedition follows modern practice, inspectors have authority, Sandefjord receives catch figures, and tanker conversion has stopped.

subfiles.title: Reply to British questions about Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP control, reporting arrangements and cancellation of a whale processing ship conversion.
subfiles.summary: Borton says Japanese operators must follow whaling agreements and that SCAP representatives exercise control. Factory ships report catches to Tokyo for weekly transmission to Sandefjord. The Japanese government was ordered to cancel conversion of an oil tanker into a processing ship; it will be completed as a tanker hull. Page 170 repeats the end of the draft.

subfiles.title: Weekly Report on Japanese Whaling Activities, November 17–23
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits three Natural Resources Section reports on coastal and Antarctic whaling.
subfiles.summary: Encloses catch, products and fleet status reports for November 17–23.

subfiles.title: Japanese coastal whaling activities, November 17–23
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Lists land stations, catchers and operating or repairing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates coastal whaling operations by company and station, with notes on vessels undergoing repair or construction.

subfiles.title: Whale products from coastal whaling, November 17–23
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports whale catches and quantities of oil, meat and other products.
subfiles.summary: Records 48 whales captured and tabulates products by company.

subfiles.title: Antarctic whaling fleet status, November 17–23
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Records vessels, tonnage, location, work and completion estimates for the Antarctic fleet.
subfiles.summary: Nippon Suisan's listed ships are complete and at sea for Antarctica. Taiyo Gyogyo's report includes factory ships, catchers and carriers, alongside vessels still under construction or repair at Shimonoseki, Nagasaki and Senshu.

subfiles.title: Weekly Report on Japanese Whaling Activities, November 24–30
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits the next three weekly reports on Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Encloses coastal activities, whale products and Antarctic fleet status reports for November 24–30.

subfiles.title: Japanese coastal whaling activities, November 24–30
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Lists coastal stations, operating catchers and inactive vessels.
subfiles.summary: Reports whaling operations at stations including Kiritappu, Kamaishi, Ayukawa, Kabashima, Senzaki and Kushiro. It notes transfers among stations and vessels under repair or construction.

subfiles.title: Whale products from coastal whaling, November 24–30
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates coastal catches and resulting products by company.
subfiles.summary: Gives whale and product figures submitted by the Japanese Bureau of Fisheries on December 4.

subfiles.title: Antarctic whaling fleet status, November 24–30
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Updates completion and repair status of remaining fleet vessels.
subfiles.summary: Reports several Taiyo vessels completed and the San Diego Maru tanker nearing completion; other fleet vessels are en route.

subfiles.title: File charge-out sheet
subfiles.about: Records removal of file material for reference.
subfiles.summary: Charge-out form identifies a whaling file and related Tokyo telegram.

subfiles.title: Flag of Antarctic Whaling Expedition
subfiles.about: Records British concern over the expedition flying the Japanese merchant marine flag.
subfiles.summary: Graves sought clarification; Emerson explained that the SCAJAP flag combined the merchant marine flag with a modified international E.

subfiles.title: Proposal to stop forwarding coastal whaling reports
subfiles.about: Proposes ending duplicate transmission of coastal whaling reports.
subfiles.summary: Natural Resources Section wishes to stop sending two coastal reports to the mission because Washington receives the information through other channels.

subfiles.title: Weekly Report on Japanese Whaling Activities, December 1–7
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits three reports for the first week of December.
subfiles.summary: Encloses coastal whaling, whale products and Antarctic fleet status reports for December 1–7.

subfiles.title: Japanese coastal whaling activities, December 1–7
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Lists coastal whaling stations, catcher movements and inactive vessels.
subfiles.summary: The report covers Nippon Suisan, Taiyo Gyogyo and Kyokuyo Hogei operations. It tracks movements among stations and vessels under repair or construction. The OCR shows overlapping copies of its pages.

subfiles.title: Whale products from coastal whaling, December 1–7
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates catches and whale products for the reporting week.
subfiles.summary: Two poorly read pages give company figures for catches and products.

subfiles.title: Antarctic whaling fleet status, December 1–7
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Updates completion and repair of vessels assigned to the Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: Two poorly read copies of the status table list completed vessels and work on an oil tanker.

subfiles.title: Request to change the Antarctic expedition's flag
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asks SCAP to consider flying only the modified international E on whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: State cites assurances to Britain and Australia that the expedition would use a SCAJAP pennant. Australia objects to the Japanese flag appearing separately, fearing a precedent for renewed Japanese Antarctic whaling. State asks SCAP to consider prohibiting the Japanese merchant marine flag and prescribing the modified international E alone.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of instructions to whaling fleet representatives
subfiles.about: Confirms SCAP representatives aboard both factory ships received instructions.
subfiles.summary: Repeats an earlier message explaining delayed mail delivery and confirms radio acknowledgment from both factory ships.

subfiles.title: Referral of whaling employment inquiry
subfiles.about: Refers a correspondent's whaling employment letter for consideration and reply.
subfiles.summary: Deason forwards the letter after speaking with Dr. Van Zant.

subfiles.title: Application to manage a whaling factory ship
subfiles.about: Offers maritime and whaling experience if the United States takes over factory ships.
subfiles.summary: Larsen seeks a master or manager position aboard a factory ship. He cites whaling service, Norwegian and Panamanian licenses, and United States Navy service.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mr. Larsen's factory ship inquiry
subfiles.from: William I. S. Feeney, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds to an offer to operate a whaling factory vessel.
subfiles.summary: States that no American operation is planned, while retaining Larsen's suggestion should a vessel transfer to the American flag.

subfiles.title: SCAP response on the expedition flag
subfiles.about: Requests international notice before ordering the fleet to fly only the modified E.
subfiles.summary: SCAP argues that a registry flag on supervised Japanese ships does not establish a precedent for future whaling. It will prohibit the merchant marine flag once the modified E alone receives appropriate international promulgation.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Glossary of Japanese Fisheries Terms
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Encloses five copies of Natural Resources Section Report No. 63.
subfiles.summary: Sends the Glossary of Japanese Fisheries Terms to Washington.

subfiles.title: Glossary of Japanese Fisheries Terms, Report No. 63
subfiles.about: Standardizes English translations and scientific identifications for Japanese fisheries vocabulary.
subfiles.summary: The introduction explains that varied Japanese names and inconsistent translations complicate fisheries reports. Captain Richard S. Croker prepared the glossary using earlier American and Japanese lists, reference works and advice from Japanese specialists. The alphabetical entries shown run from A through early O and cover aquatic species, prepared seafood, fishing gear, vessels, facilities and fisheries administration. The glossary continues beyond page 234.
